answer: Divergent-Challenge Attestation. Each agent must periodically answer a random challenge whose correct output depends on its private, evolving interaction history—its "oasis" of state. Clones share identical history, so they return identical answers. Validators request answers through a "bridge" node and compare; matching answers from distinct identities flag a clone cluster. To survive, an attacker must inject unique "timber"—distinct real interactions—into every clone, costing full per-identity operational overhead, not one shared cost.
